'''Karami''' is an extinct and unclassified [[Papuan language]] of southern [[Papua New Guinea]]. It is attested from only a short word list, which include many loans from [[Foia Foia language|Foia Foia]].<ref name=loans>Usher, Timothy. [https://newguineaworld.linguistik.uzh.ch/families/trans-new-guinea/fly-river/inland-gulf Inland Gulf family]{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}. ''New Guinea World''.</ref>

==Geographical distribution==
According to Flint (1919: 96), from which the only existing word list of Karami is available, Karami was spoken in the villages of Kikimairi and Aduahai, both located near [[Daru]] Station, "on the right-hand side (in the bush) of left branch of the [[Turama River]], [[Western Province (Papua New Guinea)|Western Division]], [[Papua New Guinea|Papua]]."<ref name="Flint-Karami"/>

==Classification==
Although Franklin (1968; 1973: 269-273) classifies Karami as an [[Inland Gulf languages|Inland Gulf]] language,<ref>Franklin, Karl J. 1968. Languages of the Gulf District: A preview. ''Papers in New Guinea Linguistics'' 8:17‒44. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics.</ref><ref>Franklin, Karl J. 1973. Other language groups in the Gulf District and adjacent areas. In ''The linguistic situation in the Gulf District and adjacent areas, Papua New Guinea'', ed. by Karl J. Franklin, 263‒77. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics.</ref> Usher and Suter (2015: 125) do not consider it to be part of the [[Anim languages]], noting that there are many loanwords from [[Foia Foia language|Foia Foia]].<ref name="Usher-Suter">Timothy Usher and Edgar Suter (2015) "The Anim Languages of Southern New Guinea". ''Oceanic Linguistics'' 54:110–142</ref>

Pawley and Hammarström (2018) treat Karami as a 'language isolate', though this is the wording used for languages that are not easily classified.<ref name="Pawley-TNG">{{cite book |last1=Pawley |first1=Andrew |last2=Hammarström |first2=Harald |editor1-last=Palmer |editor1-first=Bill |date=2018 |title=The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide |chapter=The Trans New Guinea family |series= The World of Linguistics |volume=4 |location=Berlin |publisher=De Gruyter Mouton |pages=21–196 |isbn=978-3-11-028642-7}}</ref>
